subject: iot
title: Unit 4 — TinyML, Time-Series & Predictive Maintenance Flashcards

cards.back: Running **ML inference on microcontrollers** / ultra-low-power devices (KB memory, mW power). Benefits: **low latency, offline, bandwidth-saving, privacy, low power** — intelligence pushed to the edge.

cards.front: TinyML: where do training vs inference happen?
cards.back: **Train in the cloud** (heavy, TensorFlow/PyTorch); **infer on the device**. You never train on the MCU — it lacks the compute. TinyML = efficient on-device inference of a compressed model.

Shrinking model weights (e.g., 32-bit floats → **8-bit integers**) + pruning, so the model fits KB of memory and runs fast on an MCU, usually with small accuracy loss. Tools: TF Lite for Microcontrollers, Edge Impulse.

cards.front: Why a time-series DB (InfluxDB) for IoT?
cards.back: Optimized for **high-rate timestamped writes**, **native time-range aggregation** ('avg per 5 min'), and **retention/downsampling** (keep raw briefly, summaries forever). Beats relational DBs for the (timestamp, value, tags) firehose.

Open-source platform to **visualize time-series** as live dashboards (graphs, gauges) and fire **alerts** on threshold breaches. Data-source agnostic (InfluxDB, Prometheus…). Implements pipeline stages visualize → action.
**InfluxDB (store) + Grafana (visualize + alert)**. InfluxDB = memory; Grafana = eyes. Devices write readings to InfluxDB; Grafana charts them live and alerts when something's wrong.

cards.front: Reactive vs preventive vs predictive maintenance?
cards.back: **Reactive** = fix after failure (downtime). **Preventive** = fixed calendar (too early/late). **Predictive** = fix exactly when sensor data says — the cost/safety sweet spot (only IoT data enables it).

cards.front: Predictive maintenance: the full IoT loop?
cards.back: **Sense** (vibration/temp/current, U2) → **transmit** (MQTT, U3) → **store** (InfluxDB) → **analyse** (anomaly detection / **RUL regression** / classification, U4) → **act** (auto-schedule, alert). The capstone of the whole course.

cards.front: ML techniques used in predictive maintenance?
cards.back: **Anomaly detection** (autoencoder → abnormal vibration), **regression** (predict **RUL** = Remaining Useful Life), **classification** (healthy/degrading/faulty).
**Data imbalance** (failures are rare → few positive examples), **model drift** (sensor behaviour changes → retrain via feedback loop), needing enough **historical failure data**.
